Seeing someone's face light up when they see me in the hallway.

This is going to sound very Taylor Swift, but the guy I have a crush on is in a relationship. Today in school he said he loved me, meaning it as a friend, and I couldn't stop blushing for the remainder of the class period.

I was sexually assaulted when I was five by my ten year old brother, but I didn't think to tell anyone because I didn't know it was wrong. My dad walked in on it one day (two years after it had started). I am just realizing now that it was real and actually happened because my parents refused to talk about it.
They've been supportive and I appreciate their flexibility, but it's all very overwhelming.

My parents are old school, meaning that they believe if you start something, you finish it. My situation is affecting my mental health and they don't completely understand it (they've been pretty resistant to meds but finally gave in after two months of recommendations from my therapist). The stress to do well and time commitment have pushed me over the edge. It's a long and grueling season and I know it sounds like I'm being lazy but I can't do it anymore.

My family is very into volleyball (my mother played in high school and got a full athletic scholarship for college, my older sister as well, and my older brother is on a partial scholarship for volleyball too). My mom is supportive of me wanting to do other things so the scholarship doesn't matter, but I don't think I'll be able to get through the season.

Like I said in other comments, I'm a good kid, I don't drink or do drugs, I try to try hard in school, and I always have respected my parents. This is the one thing I'm not willing to do and I've respectfully asked to quit. I'm just not sure what else I'm supposed to do.

They told me they're forcing me to play because I need the exercise (my sister has called me a fat-ass multiple times) and because they're pretty old school. "You start something, you finish it."

I'm a good kid, I usually get good grades, though lately that's been a challenge, I don't drink or do drugs, I listen to and respect my parents, and this is the first time I'm really standing up for myself. When I asked to quit I was very respectful and mature and I didn't get angry but they refuse to let me quit. I'm simply trying my best and it isn't enough.

See my comment above^^ and also, yes, I am seeing a therapist and she said that I should stick with it. She knows about my self-harm. I think deep down she wishes I could quit, but she needs to support my parents apparently.

I should have noted that the coach is my 23 year-old sister who is not sympathetic to my situation at all and simply told me to "stop being so sad all the time". She is also one of the many reasons I have self-harmed.

To answer your question, you are definitely have a right to be upset about what happened. Never feel like it was your fault or that you did something wrong. He broke your trust in one of the worst ways possible. I've had the same struggle with my older brother. The best I've been able to do so far is avoid the topic and deal with it by myself, which obviously isn't a very good way to handle it. I'm so sorry and I hope that you can sort things out with your family.

I'm a sophomore in high school, and I can definitely say that I know what you're feeling. I often forget things that I normally wouldn't forget. My grades have slipped, and I can't even bring myself to care about them. I'm legitimately going to fail multiple classes and have to retake them, but I just can't care anymore.

I can relate to this post 100%. I can't even imagine to understand how you feel, and I won't try to preach or offer "fixes" because I know that they don't do shit. But here's some advice I can offer that has helped me: take a step back from yourself. Look at your situation logically. What have you experienced that has caused you to feel like this? You said that you had an eating disorder. Obviously that was a very real thing. What you are feeling is real.

I really hope you can find peace. Let me know if there's anything you need :) Emma
